paper.title: TBATS in smooth: formulation, rationale and performance on the M4 hourly data

definitions.definition: TBATS of the smooth package (R tbats(), Python TBATS), a linear single-source-of-error model in the Box-Cox space: y_t^(lambda) = w' v_{t-l} + e_t, v_t = F v_{t-l} + g e_t, with an ETS(A,N,N), ETS(A,A,N) or ETS(A,Ad,N) level and trend, and for each period m_i and harmonic j = 1..k_i (lambda_ij = 2 pi j / m_i) two states with lags 1 and 2 in the ARIMA slot of ADAM's core: u_t = v_{1,t-1} + v_{2,t-2}, v_{k,t} = eta_k u_t + g_k e_t with eta = (2 cos lambda_ij, -1) and g = (gamma_1i, sin(lambda_ij) gamma_2i - cos(lambda_ij) gamma_1i), so that (1 - 2 cos lambda_ij B + B^2) u_t = (g_1 B + g_2 B^2) e_t; an optional ADAM ARMA component (an additive state block, not ARMA errors); lambda in [0, 1] estimated by likelihood with the Jacobian; harmonics preselected by information criterion on a global OLS model of the Box-Cox series on Fourier terms; trend and ARMA orders selected by AICc.

TBATS of De Livera, Hyndman and Snyder (2011, JASA): y_t^(lambda) = l_{t-1} + phi b_{t-1} + sum_i sum_j s^(i)_{j,t-1} + d_t, l_t = l_{t-1} + phi b_{t-1} + alpha d_t, b_t = phi b_{t-1} + beta d_t, s^(i)_{j,t} = cos(lambda_ij) s^(i)_{j,t-1} + sin(lambda_ij) s*^(i)_{j,t-1} + gamma_1i d_t, s*^(i)_{j,t} = -sin(lambda_ij) s^(i)_{j,t-1} + cos(lambda_ij) s*^(i)_{j,t-1} + gamma_2i d_t, with ARMA(p, q) errors d_t = sum phi_k d_{t-k} + sum theta_k e_{t-k} + e_t.

The tbats() function of the R package forecast (Hyndman et al.), De Livera et al.'s TBATS with its own model selection, called with seasonal.periods = c(24, 168), single-threaded, otherwise default settings.
AutoTBATS of the Python package statsforecast (Nixtla), called with season_length = [24, 168], otherwise default settings.
ADAM ETS of smooth's Python port, ADAM(model='ZXZ', lags=[24, 168]) with its default settings: ETS with a daily and a weekly seasonal component selected by AICc.
Seasonal naive forecast repeating the last 168 observations (the last week) of the training sample.

The 414 hourly series of the M4 competition (Makridakis et al., 2020), training samples of 700 or 960 observations and test samples of 48, from the Mcompetitions/M4-methods repository (Dataset/Train/Hourly-train.csv, Dataset/Test/Hourly-test.csv).
The M4 hourly training samples with their last 48 observations held out as a validation test: fitting on observations 1..n-48 and evaluating on n-47..n; never the official test samples.
Each method is fitted once to each training sample and forecasts h = 1..48 steps ahead from its end; no refits, no rolling origin.
Mean absolute scaled error of a series: mean over h = 1..48 of |y_{n+h} - f_{n+h}| divided by the in-sample mean absolute seasonal difference at lag 24, as in M4.
Geometric mean over series of MASE(method A)/MASE(method B); below 1 means A is more accurate. Its 95% confidence interval is exp of the t-interval of the mean log ratio over series.
Share of the 414 x 48 test values inside the 95% prediction interval of a method.
Wall-clock seconds to fit a method to one training sample and produce its forecasts and intervals, single-threaded.

Deterministic checks of smooth TBATS against its specification, per seed: (H1) random parameters, initial states and series of 300 observations simulated by De Livera's recursion with normal errors, for the periods {24}, {7.3}, {24, 168}, {7.3, 30.4}, no/additive/damped trend and lambda in {1, 0.5, 0}, fitted by smooth TBATS with all parameters and initial states fixed; (H2) a noise-free series of 300 observations made of a random level and random harmonics of the periods 7.3 and 24, fitted with random fixed persistence and initial='backcasting'; (H3) nine random pairs of alpha in (0.05, 0.95) and |phi| in (0.05, 0.95) for a local level with AR(1), the impulse response w'F^(j-1)g at j = 1..20 read from the fitted model's matrices. Code: claimset-code/smooth-tbats/formulation_checks.py.

The Nemenyi test of greybox's rmcb (Python port of R's greybox::rmcb, distribution='tukey', ties averaged): the methods are ranked within each series by the error measure the plan names (MASE under PL3, RMSSE from PL4 on), and two methods differ at level 1 - alpha when their mean ranks over series differ by more than the critical distance q_{1-alpha}(k, inf) / sqrt(2) * sqrt(k (k + 1) / (6 N)), for k methods and N series.

Root mean squared scaled error of a series: sqrt(mean over h = 1..48 of (y_{n+h} - f_{n+h})^2) divided by sqrt(mean over t = 2..n of (y_t - y_{t-1})^2), the in-sample root mean squared first difference, as in M5.
Geometric mean over series of RMSSE(method A)/RMSSE(method B); below 1 means A is more accurate. Its 99% confidence interval is exp of the t-interval of the mean log ratio over series.

The 370 hourly series of electricity consumption (kW) of clients of a Portuguese utility in GluonTS's electricity_nips archive (SR3), drawn from UCI ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014: each series is the archive's training series extended by its last test window, ending 2014-09-08 01:00, 1249 to 6001 hours long.

Seven daily forecast origins over the last week of each series: the last one 48 hours before its end, the others 24, 48, ..., 144 hours earlier. At each origin each method is fitted to the 1008 preceding hours (six weeks) and forecasts 48 hours ahead; the RMSSE and the interval coverage of a series are averaged over its seven origins.

[[TM1:smooth TBATS]] with the normal distribution of the error term in the space of the transformed data: TBATS(lags=[1, 24, 168], distribution="dnorm") of the Python smooth package, every other setting at its default. The default, distribution="auto", selects the structure with the generalised normal distribution (dgnorm) and then fits the closest of the normal, Laplace and S distributions on it; dnorm selects and fits with the normal distribution only.

evidence.description: Lab runs RN8 under plan PL3. Design: One run of claimset-code/smooth-tbats/m4_hourly.py --train SR1 --test SR2 --split test --workers 4 on the code branch's committed code (commit 3444dda or later with the same script), with the software of DC3: each of smooth TBATS (TBATS(lags=[1, 24, 168]) with its defaults, h = 48, 95% prediction intervals), forecast::tbats (D3), AutoTBATS (D4), ADAM ETS (D5) and seasonal naive 168 (D6) is fitted once to each of the 414 M4 hourly training samples and forecasts the 48 test values (D9), each fit single-threaded, the series spread over 4 worker processes (forecast::tbats in R first, then the Python methods). A method that fails on a series (an error or non-finite forecasts) gets the seasonal naive 168 forecasts for it and no interval, its test values counting as uncovered; the failures are reported per method. Analysis: Per series and method: MASE (D10), the coverage of the 95% prediction interval (D12), the elapsed time (D13). Relative MASE (D11) of smooth TBATS to each comparator with its 99% t-interval on the log scale, the relative elapsed time to forecast::tbats likewise; four one-sided t-tests on the mean log ratios at alpha = 0.01 (H4: vs forecast::tbats, H0 log ratio >= log 1.05; H5: vs AutoTBATS, same; H6: vs seasonal naive 168, H0 >= 0; H7: time vs forecast::tbats, H0 >= 0), their p-values adjusted by Holm over the four. The coverage of smooth TBATS over all 414 x 48 test values (H8). The Nemenyi test (D15, rmcb, level 0.99) on the per-series MASE of the five methods: mean ranks and critical distance (H9). Also reported, not deciding: mean and median MASE, mean sMAPE, median time and failures per method, the relative MASE to ADAM ETS, and rmcb's p-value of equal mean ranks.
